analysis:
The PR changes CI routing in .github/workflows/ci.yml and the matching docs in docs/developer/build.md. In ci.yml (head lines 43-47), the single `test-provider` lane with count 5 becomes five lanes, `test-provider-1` to `test-provider-5`, each with count 1. In the `test-provider` job (head line 142), `runs-on` now reads `fromJSON(needs.route.outputs.routes)[format('test-provider-{0}', matrix.shard)]`. The matrix shard values 1-5 match the lane names. The route job keeps `permissions: {}`, and the other workflow permissions are unchanged (`contents: read`). Action pins are unchanged. No secrets, token permissions, trigger events or artifact flows change. The change only affects whether each read-only provider test shard lands on a Darkbloom Sandbox or on the Blacksmith fallback.

Security-relevant considerations:
- Routing is handled by darkbloom-route.yml, which is not in the supplied evidence. The docs say grants are used only when they repeat the exact labels, and that errors keep the fallback. I could not verify that behavior.
- A missing lane key would fall back to an empty `runs-on` and fail the job. That is an availability issue, not a security one.
- No threat-model asset, boundary or threat (A-001..A-019, TB-002..TB-013, T-041 and related) is touched. CI runs the provider test suite and does not alter provider code, the attestation path, key custody or the coordinator wire protocol.
- Running tests on Darkbloom Sandbox Macs is a pre-existing design. The shard split gives more jobs a chance to be placed on sandbox runners. Any trust implications of the sandbox plane (TB-013) are outside this diff.

No regressions were identified. The remaining integration question is the darkbloom-route.yml lane parsing and its handling of the new per-lane counts, which I did not review.
